notes.text: Performance data is based on testing in accordance with ASHRAE Standard 70, Method of Testing for Rating the Performance of Air Outlets and Inlets.

Sound levels are listed as NC and are based on a room absorption of 10 dB re 10-12 watts with a single diffuser. Adjust listed values for actual room absorption and the number of outlets serving the space.
NC values listed as "<15" indicate a sound level below NC 15.
All pressures are listed in inches water gauge (in. w.g.). Total pressure equals static pressure plus velocity pressure.
Finish shall be B12 standard white unless otherwise noted. Optional colors, custom colors, and Armstrong coordinated finishes are available; confirm lead time with the manufacturer.

Frame and border style shall match the ceiling system indicated on the architectural reflected ceiling plans. Contractor shall verify ceiling type, module size, and ceiling opening dimensions prior to release for fabrication.

Provide each diffuser with a volume control damper unless served by a terminal unit or otherwise noted. Provide radial or full flow damper (VCR7, VCR8, VCR8E, or VCR9) at round inlets and opposed blade damper (VCS3) at square or rectangular inlets. Some damper models are not available at all inlet sizes; verify availability with the submittal.
Dampers, air baffles, and light shields ship loose and shall be field installed by the installing contractor.

Provide insulated backpan where diffusers are located in unconditioned or high humidity plenums. Provide molded backpan insulation (R6, frame A profile only) or foil backed fiberglass insulation (AFI, frame B profile only) as required by the application.
Provide beaded inlet neck with 2-1/2 in. extended depth (BN) where flexible duct connections are used. Beaded neck is not available on aluminum construction units.
Provide extended hanger tabs (EHT) in lieu of standard integral hanger loops where required by the installation.

Where diffusers occur in a fire rated ceiling assembly, provide fire rated construction incorporating a thermal blanket and fire damper, UL listed and meeting NFPA 90A. Fusible link shall be 165 deg F unless otherwise noted. Listed performance does not include the effect of a ceiling radiation damper.
Diffuser sizes, neck sizes, and airflows shown are for bidding purposes. Contractor shall coordinate final selections with approved terminal unit and ductwork submittals.
Throw is listed in feet to terminal velocities of 150 fpm (minimum), 100 fpm (middle), and 50 fpm (maximum), shown in the schedule as 150-100-50.

Throw data is based on supply air and room air at isothermal conditions, except SCDA vertical throw, which is based on a 20 deg F heating differential at 50 fpm terminal velocity. Adjust listed throw for the scheduled heating or cooling temperature differential.
Published performance is for supply air applications with the diffuser ceiling mounted for maximum ceiling effect.
Diffuser shall discharge a 360 degree radial horizontal air pattern for rapid mixing and temperature equalization.
Diffuser is suitable for high turndown VAV service; the horizontal discharge pattern is maintained at reduced air volumes to minimize dumping and drafts.
Diffuser shall have a one piece aerodynamic backpan and a tool free removable face for access to the damper, accessories, and ductwork.

Where a 1-way, 2-way, 2-way corner, or 3-way discharge pattern is indicated on the drawings, provide air baffles (AB); baffles ship loose for field installation. Standard construction without baffles discharges a 360 degree radial horizontal pattern.
Steel construction (SPD) is standard. Provide aluminum construction (ASPD) where required by the specification or corrosive environment.

Where a 1-way, 2-way, or 3-way discharge pattern is indicated on the drawings, provide a sectorizing baffle (SB-270 for 1-way, SB-180 for 2-way, SB-90 for 3-way). Sectorizing baffles are not available in combination with any factory damper selection; provide a field furnished duct mounted damper where volume control is also required.
Diffuser shall have an aerodynamic backpan and cone assembly that minimizes low pressure areas at the face to reduce ceiling smudging.
Diffuser shall be furnished with adjustable pattern controllers permitting field adjustment between horizontal and vertical discharge.
Scheduled horizontal and vertical values represent the two pattern controller positions. Balance to the discharge pattern indicated on the drawings.

Provide removable core (RC) unless a fixed core (FC) is scheduled. Fixed core is available on 24 in. x 24 in. lay-in (style 3) units only. Optional fourth cone (4C) is available on 24 in. x 24 in. units only.
Vertical discharge is intended for heating applications and high ceiling installations. Verify listed vertical throw against the scheduled mounting height.
Core style determines the discharge pattern (1-way through 4-way). Provide the core style scheduled. Cores are removable at the diffuser face without special tools.
Listed airflow per side and throw apply to each active side of the diffuser. Side A and Side B values are listed separately where the core style discharges unequal airflow.
Where no ceiling is present, horizontal throw is reduced by approximately 25 percent and the discharge projects downward. Coordinate diffuser selection at exposed structure locations.

Where the diffuser is applied in return service, multiply the listed total pressure by the published return factor for the scheduled duct size to obtain negative static pressure, and apply the published NC correction.

Provide adjustable pattern deflectors (SMDA/AMDA) where field adjustment between horizontal and vertical discharge is required. Apply the manufacturer's published SMDA/AMDA performance correction factors.
Steel construction (SMD) is standard. Provide aluminum construction (AMD) where required by the specification or corrosive environment.
Diffuser shall be furnished with round inlet (SR) sized to the scheduled round duct. Performance for the SMD with SR is per the manufacturer's published SMD/AMD with SR data.
Listed static pressure and sound include the square to round adapter. Listed throw is based on a 4-way discharge pattern.
Coordinate the round duct connection to the SR inlet with the installing contractor prior to setting the ceiling.
Return performance is listed as negative static pressure at the scheduled airflow. Throw values are not applicable to return applications.
Return diffuser face and border style shall match the associated supply diffuser for a consistent ceiling appearance.
Return diffuser shall be the same square plaque face as the supply diffuser, furnished without air baffles (AB).
Perforated face shall be 3/16 in. diameter perforations with 51 percent free area, matching the perforated supply diffusers in appearance and detail.
Face panel shall be hinged and removable with quick release spring latches for access to the damper and ductwork.

Units scheduled as "Ducted" shall be furnished with the scheduled neck size and a duct connection. Units scheduled as "Plenum Return" draw air directly from the ceiling cavity and are furnished with an oversized inlet.

Provide a light shield (LS) at plenum return applications to minimize sightlines into the ceiling cavity. Light shield is available with square or rectangular inlets only, is not available in combination with a damper, and is not available on the 46 in. x 22 in. inlet size.
Provide extended face construction (frame style 15) where required to align the diffuser face flush with tegular ceiling tile; the face extends 3/8 in. below the t-bar plane.
Where the return diffuser is mounted directly to a duct branch or fitting, coordinate inlet conditions to provide uniform face velocity across the diffuser face.
